name: Kerala Arts & Crafts Village (KACV), Vellar
tagline: State craft village at Vellar — live studios, curated emporium and cultural shows near Kovalam
summary: A state-supported craft village at Vellar (near Kovalam) that hosts 100+ artisan studios, live demonstrations in coir, shell, wood and metal, a curated emporium and evening performances.
description: Kerala Arts & Crafts Village (KACV) at Vellar, near Kovalam, is an 8.5-acre cultural campus developed as a state tourism craft village to revive and market Kerala’s traditional crafts. The site is an initiative of the Department of Tourism and was designed and developed by Uralungal Labour Contract Co‑operative Society (ULCCS).

The village groups working studios, a handloom zone, galleries, an amphitheatre and a curated emporium where artisans sell coir and coconut‑husk pieces, shell and metalwork, carved wood, mural paintings and handloom textiles. Visitors see makers at work and can buy directly from craft studios.

KACV also programmes workshops, daily demonstrations and evening performances (classical, folk and martial arts) in its open amphitheatre; the site positions itself as a cultural exchange hub for festivals, design labs and craft fairs.
For travellers it combines short, hands‑on craft experiences with gift shopping and regular cultural events — a practical one-stop place to learn about Kerala craft traditions while visiting Kovalam.
highlights: Curated emporium selling coir, coconut‑husk, shell, wood and metal crafts
Working artisan studios — watch live demonstrations and meet makers
Handloom village showcasing Balaramapuram and other Kerala weaves
Open amphitheatre with evening cultural programmes and Kalaripayattu showcases
Workshops and short craft experiences for visitors and groups
Close to Kovalam and Trivandrum (airport ~13 km, railway ~12 km)

sections.heading: Background
body: KACV is a state tourism initiative created to conserve, demonstrate and market Kerala’s craft traditions. The campus spreads across about 8.5 acres at Vellar (Vazhamuttom), Kovalam and was designed and implemented with support from the Uralungal Labour Contract Co‑operative Society (ULCCS).
The village houses more than 100 artisans and studios, and the model emphasises direct artisan livelihoods, ethical procurement and responsible‑tourism practices.

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: Walk the studios to see coir and coconut‑husk craft, brass‑embroidered coconut shell work, carved wooden boxes (Nettur petti), metalwork and Kerala mural art. The handloom area explains local weaves such as Balaramapuram; artists are usually willing to explain techniques and materials.

Shop at the curated emporium for authentic handicrafts, join short workshops (pottery, weaving, quilling or doll‑making when scheduled), and attend the amphitheatre evening shows — many performances centre on Kalaripayattu, classical dance and folk music.

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: KACV is a short drive from Trivandrum International Airport (about 13 km) and the city railway station (about 12 km); it sits en route to Kovalam so you can combine a beach visit. The official site lists the village address and contact for bookings — confirm timings and any entry or workshop fees before you travel.

The village runs regular events and seasonal festivals; larger programmes (for example cultural weeks and dance festivals) are announced on the KACV site and by the Tourism Department. If you plan a group visit or a workshop, call or email ahead to reserve.

latest.text: KACV hosts its International Dance Festival and a programme of performances and workshops in November 2026 — the village is active as an event venue through the season (check the current events calendar before visiting).

Government sanctions funding (₹35,00,000) for 'WOW WEEK — World of Women’s Week 2026' at the Kerala Arts & Crafts Village (events held 2–8 March 2026), highlighting festivalisation and women‑centric craft programming.

Government sanctions financial assistance (₹80,00,000) for two flagship cultural programmes — Meythari and Attachuvadu — presented at KACV, underlining the site’s role in responsible tourism and Kalaripayattu programming.

visitorInfo.bestTime: October–March (dry season and festival months); check event calendar for scheduled performances.
visitorInfo.howToReach: From Trivandrum International Airport ~13 km (20–30 minutes by taxi); from Thiruvananthapuram Railway Station ~12 km. The village sits at Vellar, Kovalam — local buses stop at Vellar Junction and the site is a short walk from the bus stop. Confirm directions with KACV before travel.
etiquette: Call or email ahead to confirm opening hours, entry fees and workshop availability (times vary and some programmes run on selected days).
Bring a reusable bag — many items are eco‑materials (coir, coconut shell) and packaging is often minimal.
If you want custom pieces or larger purchases, speak directly to the maker; many studios accept orders but lead times can be several weeks.
Respect studio spaces: ask before photographing close‑up of makers or their tools, and follow any safety instructions in working areas.
